provenance_states.name: Observed
provenance_states.description: Read directly from a source artifact. Seen, not concluded.

provenance_states.name: Inferred
provenance_states.description: Concluded from evidence rather than seen. Always carries a confidence, is never presented as established fact, and may never block delivery.

provenance_states.name: Human Verified
provenance_states.description: A named human checked this and signed off, with a timestamp.

provenance_states.name: Certified
provenance_states.description: Human-verified and additionally passed a formal evaluation or governance gate. The only state trusted for high-risk automated action.

evaluation_scenarios.name: NFR and Integration Coverage
evaluation_scenarios.expected_behavior: The architecture document addresses every stated NFR and names every integration point.

evaluation_scenarios.name: Vendor-Neutral Choice
evaluation_scenarios.expected_behavior: Capability choices are justified independently of a specific vendor.

evaluation_scenarios.name: Cost Estimate Present
evaluation_scenarios.expected_behavior: Cost implications are estimated, even though ARC-04 is not mandatory.

evaluation_scenarios.name: Full Impact Coverage
evaluation_scenarios.expected_behavior: Given a change touching N assets, the selected test set covers all N.

evaluation_scenarios.name: Low False Positive Rate
evaluation_scenarios.expected_behavior: A stable, unrelated change does not trigger unnecessary test selection.

evaluation_scenarios.name: Respects Test Readiness Gate
evaluation_scenarios.expected_behavior: Test evidence produced satisfies gate.test-readiness's evidence requirements.

capabilities.name: Data Modelling

capabilities.name: Data Profiling
capabilities.description: Measuring the statistical shape of data -- volume, null rates, cardinality, distributions.

changes: 66 entity types across the Technical Twin, the Delivery Twin, the organization, capability, work, evaluation, platform and context.
Relationships as first-class provenanced objects; 63 types, of which 19 are cross-twin joins.
Four-state provenance with executable invariants, plus document provenance (source_document, source_section, extraction_method).
Blockable mixin - an INFERRED rule cannot block delivery until verified.
Four-level role chain via first-class EngineeringResponsibility.
Technical and delivery capabilities as distinct catalogs.

engineering_responsibilities.name: Impact Assessment
engineering_responsibilities.statement: Determine, before a change lands, exactly which assets, pipelines, capabilities and consumers it affects, with evidence for each claim.

engineering_responsibilities.name: Regression Proof
engineering_responsibilities.statement: Prove that a change does not break existing behaviour, by selecting and running the smallest sufficient set of tests.

engineering_responsibilities.name: Data Correctness
engineering_responsibilities.statement: Ensure data is correct, complete and fit for its declared purpose.

engineering_responsibilities.name: Logical Data Design
engineering_responsibilities.statement: Define the logical representation of required data, traceable to business requirements and conformant to enterprise data standards.

engineering_responsibilities.name: Architecture Integrity
engineering_responsibilities.statement: Ensure the solution structure remains coherent and fit for purpose.

engineering_responsibilities.name: Architecture Sign-off
engineering_responsibilities.statement: Accept, on the organization's behalf, that a design is fit to build. This is an accountability, not a task.

engineering_responsibilities.name: Security Assessment
engineering_responsibilities.statement: Assess data protection and access obligations against the change and produce the evidence a clearance decision needs.

engineering_responsibilities.name: Security Clearance
engineering_responsibilities.statement: Accept, on the organization's behalf, that security obligations are met. An accountability, not a task.

engineering_responsibilities.name: Release Preparation
engineering_responsibilities.statement: Assemble a release with complete evidence and the runbook needed to operate it.

engineering_responsibilities.name: Release Readiness Sign-off
engineering_responsibilities.statement: Accept that a release is fit to deploy. An accountability, not a task.

engineering_responsibilities.name: Documentation Currency
engineering_responsibilities.statement: Keep human-readable descriptions accurate as the system changes.

engineering_responsibilities.name: Requirements Quality
engineering_responsibilities.statement: Ensure requirements are unambiguous, testable, traceable and cited to a source.

engineering_responsibilities.name: Feasibility Assessment
engineering_responsibilities.statement: Assess the technical, operational and cost feasibility of a proposed solution before requirements and architecture commit resources to it. Unlike resp.architecture-signoff or resp.release-readiness this carries no non-delegable sign-off twin: the discovery phase has no formal approval gate in this delivery model, so the assessment's GO/NO-GO/ CONDITIONAL verdict is recorded directly on the produced DeliveryArtifact rather than behind a gate. See ADR-0012.

risk_classes.description: Reversible, contained, no production or customer impact.
Reversible with effort; affects a single system.
Customer-impacting, regulatory, or hard to reverse.
Irreversible, or affecting production data or access control.

action_classes.description: Creates isolated, easily discarded artifacts -- a branch, a comment, a draft.
Changes shared state -- merging code, altering a schema.
Deletes or overwrites data, or changes access control.

engineering_roles.name: Regression Engineer
engineering_roles.mission: Guarantee that a change does not silently break existing behaviour, by selecting and running the smallest sufficient set of tests.
evaluation_criteria: Selected tests cover every impacted asset
Selection is explainable against the dependency graph
Test evidence satisfies the test-readiness gate

engineering_roles.name: Impact Analysis Engineer
engineering_roles.mission: Determine, before a change lands, which assets, capabilities, consumers and delivery obligations it affects, with evidence for each claim.
evaluation_criteria: No impacted asset is missed (recall prioritised over precision)
Every impact edge carries provenance and confidence
Delivery obligations are reported alongside technical impact

engineering_roles.name: Data Quality Engineer
engineering_roles.mission: Ensure data flowing through the project is correct, complete and fit for purpose, and that violations surface before consumers see them.
evaluation_criteria: Findings cite the profiling evidence behind them
Proposed assertions are executable, not prose

engineering_roles.name: Data Model Engineer
engineering_roles.mission: Produce logical and physical data models traceable to business requirements and conformant to enterprise data standards.
evaluation_criteria: Every logical entity traces to a business requirement
Every logical entity has an identified business owner
Model conforms to enterprise naming standards

engineering_roles.name: Delivery Compliance Engineer
engineering_roles.mission: Determine whether a change complies with the organization's delivery model, and report precisely what is missing when it does not.
evaluation_criteria: Gate readiness matches the human decision that follows it
Never reports BLOCKED on an advisory-only shortfall
Every missing item names the control it came from

engineering_roles.name: Documentation Engineer
engineering_roles.mission: Keep documentation accurate as the system changes.

engineering_roles.name: Data Architect
engineering_roles.mission: Ensure the project's structure remains coherent and fit for purpose.

engineering_roles.name: Security Engineer
engineering_roles.mission: Ensure data protection and access control obligations are met.

engineering_roles.name: Release Engineer
engineering_roles.mission: Ensure releases carry complete evidence and pass the readiness gate.

engineering_roles.name: Site Reliability Engineer
engineering_roles.mission: Ensure what is released can be run, monitored and recovered.

engineering_roles.name: Requirements Engineer
engineering_roles.mission: Produce unambiguous, testable, traceable, cited requirements, and assess the feasibility of proposed solutions before they are committed to.
evaluation_criteria: Feasibility verdicts are traceable to evidence, not opinion
GO verdicts do not omit known technical or cost risk

engineering_roles.name: Governance Engineer
engineering_roles.mission: Ensure regulatory controls are implemented and demonstrable.

relationship_types.description: Structural containment -- project to asset, table to column.
A pipeline reads an asset, or an asset derives from another. The most important inferred edge in the graph -- impact analysis walks it.
A test protects an asset or pipeline. Drives impact-aware test selection.
A profiling result measured against a data asset at a point in time.
Concrete technology realizing an architecture element.
A change affects part of the technical twin. Usually INFERRED.
Phase ordering. The registry validator checks this graph is acyclic.
An input or output specification satisfied by a concrete artifact.
A task or phase validated by a checklist.
An output judged against an acceptance criterion.
Work must conform to a standard or definition of done.
A task or gate implements a governance control.
RACI assignment of a delivery role to a task, phase or gate.
A delivery contract binds everything one task needs.
A project is governed by a delivery model. The top-level join.

A delivery artifact documents technical reality. Almost always INFERRED, and the confidence matters: acting on a low-confidence DESCRIBES edge means telling someone to update a document that was never about their code.
Which delivery task owns changes to a technical thing.
A change creates a delivery obligation. The heart of dual impact analysis.
A technical test discharges an organizational evidence requirement.
A requirement is implemented by a delivery task. Head of the trace chain.
A delivery role is accountable for an engineering responsibility.
A responsibility is fulfilled by an engineering role.
An engineering role is implemented by an agent. The role outlives the agent.
A project demonstrates a capability, evidenced by discovery.
Evidence underpins a finding, decision or evaluation.
An observation proposes a correction to a twin or to knowledge.
